Teaching shows how separation protects paper and reusable containers, how reduction avoids waste, and how processing or controlled breakdown recovers material. It explains the broader legal packaging definition instead of merely naming it.

Accepted materials depend on the receiving facility; ordinary rejected wrappers are distinguished from special waste. Chemical containers must not be reused for food. Sorting without recovery is not proof of diversion, and legal recycling may overlap reuse.
